checks.finding: Terms are anchored by an explicit Field Definitions block (Cross-runtime handoff, Live-host hook-activation handshake proof, Semantic live-host matrix cell, Unicode-normalization contract, Installed-cache drift, Manual-required check, Zero-residue uninstall) and REQ-006's three-value classification vocabulary (automated / automated-pending-confirmation / manual-required) is used uniformly. I specifically re-checked OQ-002 (requirements.md:753-764) against REQ-005's Goals scope list (requirements.md:164-178) and the parallel Assumptions mention (requirements.md:737-742): all three enumerate the identical four-item scope (plugins/**, Codex agent TOML, MCP delimited block, three hook config files) with no wording drift, so two implementers reading this package would resolve REQ-005's scope identically.

No direct conflict found between Goals/Non-goals/Security Boundaries. Non-goals' verification-only framing (requirements.md:213-240) is consistent with REQ-001-REQ-004's own repeated 'never re-specifying'/'never re-authoring' language. Security Boundary B2 (requirements.md:713) claims read-only behavior only for the REQ-005 drift check specifically, which does not conflict with the disclosed design.md nonce-ledger write exception for the separate validate-live-host-proof component (a different component under B1, which requirements.md never claims is unconditionally read-only). OQ-002/REQ-005 enumeration (see AMBIGUITY finding) is internally consistent, not contradictory.

The dedicated Edge Cases section (requirements.md:672-706) and multiple ACs cover material negative/boundary paths: AC-008 idempotency (double-install), AC-009 zero-residue post-uninstall, AC-013/AC-014 explicitly-asserted non-firing states (Codex plugin_hooks disabled, Copilot subagent), AC-022 requires an independent negative-lifecycle divergence case beyond the happy path, AC-023 distinguishes not-installed/synced/drifted and flips 'not-installed' to a hard FAIL in verify mode, and AC-026/AC-027 guard against nonce reuse, hash mismatch, and single-signature self-attestation.

All four Assumptions (requirements.md:718-742) are grounded in specific investigation.md citations (INV-005/006/007 for Epic A1 status, INV-008/009 for A5/A7 status). Of the two Open Questions, OQ-001 (requirements.md:746-752) is explicitly left unresolved but is clearly marked as a Phase 2/3-confirmed gating fact never to be assumed, and OQ-002 (requirements.md:753-764) is explicitly marked resolved with a citation to design.md's Coverage Scope table. Neither assumption nor open question is left ambiguous about its own resolution status.

A human governance boundary is squarely in scope (manual-session live-host proof, AC-026/AC-027/AC-028) and is testable: Roles and Permissions (requirements.md:605-631) requires an Independent reviewer distinct from the Operator; AC-026 enumerates exact invalidity conditions (missing field, nonce reuse/absence, hash mismatch, config-digest mismatch, unverifiable signature); AC-027 forbids automated/manual substitution; and 'a record signed only by its own operator is invalid ... never a self-attested single-signature record' (requirements.md:621-622) gives an explicit, checkable rejection rule rather than an unstated norm.

acceptance-tests.md carries exactly one primary REQ per AC row for all 30 ACs (secondary dependencies, e.g. AC-005/AC-028's REQ-006 dependency, are recorded only in Test Type prose per REQ-007's own rule at requirements.md:196-201), AC-029/AC-030 correctly map to REQ-007 rather than a 'REQ (process)' placeholder, and every Test Type cell cites design.md's Classification Table directly with no leftover 'TBD' marker anywhere in the table — nothing here requires a design reviewer to invent missing product behavior.
